info.title: Tawi Studio API
info.summary: Everything the Tawi studio's web page does, for scripts and automation.
info.description:
The HTTP API behind the studio's web page: create agents, upload data, train, test, run the safety check,
publish versions and deploy them. Use it to automate what you would otherwise click through.

**Stability.** This API is versioned with the studio and can change between minor releases while the studio
is below 1.0; changes are listed in the changelog. Apps that answer customers should call the
[Agent API](https://docs.tawi.ai/api/agent) instead, which is stable.

**Signing in.** `POST /api/login` sets two cookies: `ak_session` (the session, 12 hours) and `tawi_csrf`.
Send both cookies on every request, and on every request that changes something (anything but GET) also
send the `X-CSRF-Token` header with the value of the `tawi_csrf` cookie. A temporary password (the first
`admin`/`admin`, or one an admin set) only works from the studio's own PC until it is changed.

**Names.** The API calls agents *bots* in its paths (`/api/bots/{bid}`); `bid` is the agent's 8-character id.

Guide: [Studio API guide](https://docs.tawi.ai/guides/studio-api).

post.summary: New agent from an agent file
post.description:
Create a `deploy` agent (no training, no documents) from an uploaded agent file. Its name comes from the
file's first `# heading`, or the file name.

get.description: Every agent, newest first.

post.description:
Create an agent with a model, a style (which sets the starting agent file) and a mode: `rag` (answers
from documents), `train` (fine-tuned on example Q&A), `rag_train` (both) or `deploy` (the model and the
agent file only). Models, styles and modes are listed by `GET /api/catalog`.

get.description: One agent with its settings, data, versions, safety result and API state (never the key).

patch.description:
Change any of the fields sent. Training settings in `params` are checked against their allowed ranges.
Changing the model drops the agent's versions (they belong to one base model), and is refused while a
fine-tuned version is live. Changing the mode, model, safety rules or safety source clears the last
safety check.

delete.description: Delete the agent and all its files (data, index, versions, API key). Refused while it trains.

put.description: Replace the agent file's text (up to 20,000 characters). Clears the last safety check.

post.description: The same as saving it, from an uploaded `.md` or `.txt` file.

put.description:
Requests a minute per key (1 to 10,000; null means the studio default `TAWI_RATE_PER_MIN`, 30) and an
optional daily limit for the agent (0 or null for none).

200.description: The limits in force and today's count.

post.description:
The Go live test panel: the same code path as `POST /v1/chat` with the published version, keeping a
conversation per `conversation` name (`reset: true` starts it over). Not counted as usage.

200.description: What `POST /v1/chat` would return, with the time it took.

schema.description: The same events as the Agent API's streamed chat.

get.description: The running or last speed test, or `state: idle`.

post.description:
Measure time to first word and words per second for a version (or the base model with `base_model: true`)
in a precision, in the background. The result is kept on the agent per version and precision.

Ask the agent a question from the studio's chat, with its active version (not necessarily the live one).
`side: base` asks the untrained base model without documents, for comparison. Not counted as API usage.
`stream: true` returns server-sent events like the Agent API's.

200.description: The answer, with the checks that ran and the time it took.

get.description: The agent's synced sources (never their secrets), and the kinds that can be added.

post.description:
Connect a Google Drive folder (`kind: gdrive`, with a service account key and the folder link) or Notion
pages (`kind: notion`, with an integration secret). The secret is checked, stored encrypted on this
machine, and the first sync runs before the reply. It syncs again every `every_hours` hours (0 = by hand).

delete.description: Disconnect a source and remove the documents it added.

post.description: Download new and changed files, remove deleted ones, and rebuild the index if anything changed.

get.description: Where the agent runs in Docker, the deployment in progress, and whether Docker is running on this PC.

post.description:
Build the agent's container with its live version and API key hash, and run it on this PC
(`target_id: local`) or a connected server, on `port` (1024 to 65535; not 8000 locally). Runs in the
background; follow it with `GET /api/bots/{bid}/deploy`. The API must exist first.
Stop and remove the agent's container on a server.

200.description: Whether it stopped, with the command's output.

get.description: The agent's Docker build folder as a zip, to build and run anywhere by hand.

200.description: A report per file and the new index size.

delete.description: Remove a document and rebuild the index.

post.description:
Copy an agent's settings, agent file, data and search index. Fine-tuned versions, the API key, the
safety result and usage are not copied: the copy starts as a draft.

get.description: Earlier builds of the search index, newest first, and which one is in use. An unknown agent id gets an empty list.

post.description: Put an earlier build of the search index back in use.

Publish the agent on the Agent API. The first time, this creates the API key (`ak_...`) and returns it
**once**; only its hash is stored. Later calls publish the active version and return `key: null`.

The active version must have passed the safety check on its current agent file. `skip_safety: true` goes
live without it; the choice is recorded on the agent and holds only for this version and agent file.

200.description: Live. `key` is the new API key the first time, otherwise null.

get.description: Whether the agent has an exported pipeline, its `dvc status`, and its metrics. An unknown agent id gets `exists: false`.

post.description: Write `pipelines/<id>/dvc.yaml` and `params.yaml` from the agent's current settings and commit them.

200.description: The files written and the commit.

post.description:
Upload the example questions and answers (CSV with question and answer columns, or chat JSONL) that
fine-tuning learns from. Replaces the previous file. About 10% of questions are held out (never trained
on) and become the default test questions; rows that look harmful to training are counted under
`qa.quality` without being dropped.

200.description: The file's report and the agent.

post.description:
Rewrite the examples without the flagged rows (near-empty or overlong answers, exact repeats) as
`<name>.clean.csv`. The original stays on disk next to it.

put.description:
Change the agent's search settings; fields left out keep their value and `reset: true` restores the
defaults. Changing the embedding model or chunk size rebuilds the index. Clears the last safety check.

200.description: The new settings, and whether the index was rebuilt.

get.description: How many ratings and choices the agent has, and how many preference pairs they make. Unknown agent ids return zeros.

post.description:
Record a thumbs up or down (`answer` with `rating` +1 or -1) or a choice between two answers (`chosen` and
`rejected`). Ratings feed preference tuning (`dpo_human`).

Add plain text for continued pretraining (training `kind: text`). Files that look like example Q&A are
refused with a pointer to the Q&A upload.

200.description: A report per file and the agent.

get.description: The running check's results so far, or `state: idle` with the last finished result.

post.description:
Run the red-team prompts (the built-in set, the agent's own files, or both, per `safety_source`) against
the active version in the background. The API can only go live, or publish a version, once the check
passes (`GET /api/catalog` gives the bar as `redteam_bar`).
Replace the agent's API key. The old key stops working at once; the new one is returned once.

Add your own red-team prompts (CSV; `GET /api/safety-sample.csv` shows the format). Set the agent's
`safety_source` to `custom` or `both` to use them.

200.description: The file's report and the agent.

delete.description: Remove one of the agent's safety-check files.

post.description:
A small, clean tea-shop dataset (20 Q&A pairs, and a policies document for agents that search), so a
first agent can be trained and tested end to end. Not for `deploy` agents.

200.description: The examples' report and the agent.

post.description: Version the agent's data, index and weights with DVC and commit the pointer files to git.

200.description: The commit and what was versioned.

get.description: The agent's DVC snapshots, newest first, with their commits.
The running or last generation job and its examples, or `state: idle`. Unknown agent ids also return `idle`.

post.description:
Have a teacher model (`claude`, `openai`, or the local model) write `n` examples (1 to 2,000) from a
description or from the agent's documents, in the background. Hosted teachers need their API key
(`PUT /api/providers/{name}`). Review the results, then add them with `POST /api/bots/{bid}/synth/accept`.

Add the generated examples at the indexes in `keep` to the agent's Q&A (or replace it with
`replace: true`). They get the usual quality checks and held-out split.

Save up to 20 test questions (`{"q": ..., "expected": ...}`) and answer each with both the base model and
the agent, side by side.

get.description:
The current or last run: its state (`idle`, `preparing`, `starting`, `loading`, `training`, `done`,
`failed`, `cancelled` or `interrupted`), step, loss, the loss curve so far, recent events and the GPU.
Poll it every few seconds while a run is going. An unknown agent id gets `state: idle`.

post.description:
Train a new version in the background and return at once; follow it with `GET /api/bots/{bid}/train`.
`kind` is `qa` (fine-tune on the example Q&A), `text` (continued pretraining on raw text) or `align`
(preference tuning from an existing version, with `align.method` one of `dpo_safety`, `dpo_human`,
`dpo_reference`, `dpo_ai` or `ppo`). Settings in `params` override the agent's for this run and are kept.

One GPU, one run: a second start gets 409. The GPU memory is checked first. While training, the Agent
API answers "We'll be back shortly." (search-only answers keep working). A run interrupted by a studio
restart resumes from its last checkpoint when started again.

version.description: The version this run will become.

resume.description: Resuming from a checkpoint of an interrupted run.

post.description: Stop the agent's run (its process tree is killed). The Agent API answers normally again.

get.description: The index's items a page at a time (up to 100), optionally filtered by source or by text.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only items whose text contains this (any case).

post.description: Rebuild the search index from the agent's documents and examples.

Search the index as the agent would (hybrid embeddings and keywords, then reranking) and show every hit
with its score and whether it passes the agent's threshold (`min_score`). No model call.

get.description: How many passages and Q&A items the index holds, per source, with its size, embedding model and settings.

The agent's trained versions, newest first, each with its stage (`draft`, `tested` or `live`), plus which
one is live, which one a rollback would return to, and the recent history of live changes.

post.description: Answer the saved test questions (up to 10) with versions `a` and `b`, side by side, before promoting one.

get.description: Versions `a` and `b` side by side, setting by setting and metric by metric, with their loss curves.

post.description: Serve version `v` on the Agent API. It must have passed the safety check, and the API must exist.

200.description: The new and previous live versions.

post.description: Make the previously live version live again.

delete.description: Delete a version's weights and record. The live version can't be deleted.

get.description:
Everything the studio offers: models (with memory estimates and whether they fit this GPU), styles,
modes, precisions, training engines, safety rules and limits.

post.description:
Set a new password (at least 8 characters, not `admin`), and optionally a new username. Every other
session of this account is signed out.

Delete every agent with its data, indexes, versions, API keys and experiments. Accounts, notebooks and
connected machines stay. Send `confirm: CLEAR`. Admins only.

get.description: This PC and the connected machines (SSH or AWS).

post.description: Check and save a machine (`kind` ssh or aws). Admins only.

200.description: The saved machine and the check.

delete.description: Remove a connected machine. This PC can't be removed. Admins only.

post.description: Check that a machine can be reached with the given SSH or AWS settings, without saving it. Admins only.

get.description: A machine's recent GPU readings.

post.summary: Run a command on a machine
post.description:
Run one command (up to 500 characters, 60 seconds) on a connected machine, to check its setup. Output is
capped. Not on this PC. Admins only.

200.description: The command's exit code and output.

get.description: Every training run of every agent, newest first, a page at a time (up to 2,000), with a summary of all of them.
Every run as one CSV row, for a spreadsheet.
The metric series of the chosen runs, for drawing charts in the page.
A zip with the CSV and charts of the chosen runs (all runs when `keys` is empty).
One metric for up to 6 runs as a PNG chart. `download=true` sends it as an attachment.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: The metric to plot, for example `loss`.

get.description: The local GPU's name, memory, temperature and use, and whether training or loading is going on.

post.description: Unload every model the studio holds. Waits up to 10 seconds for an answer in progress.

get.description: The models held for answering, GPU memory in use, and any training run.

post.description:
Check a username and password and start a 12-hour session. Sets the `ak_session` cookie (HttpOnly) and
the `tawi_csrf` cookie, whose value goes in the `X-CSRF-Token` header of later requests that change
something. After 10 wrong passwords from one address in 15 minutes, sign-in is refused for 15 minutes.
End this session and clear its cookies.

get.description: The last log records (up to 2,000), optionally only one level or those containing some text.
The studio's logs as a zip, to attach to a bug report.
The signed-in account, its role, and whether it must choose a new password first.
The models the studio can use, with whether each is downloaded and any download in progress.
One model's download state.

delete.description: Delete the model's downloaded files (it is unloaded first). Refused during a download.

200.description: How much was freed, and the model's status.

post.description: Record that the licence was accepted, which models with a licence gate need before downloading.
Stop the model's download. What was downloaded so far is kept for resuming.

Start downloading the model in the background (resumable, with SHA-256 checks). 403 when its licence
hasn't been accepted, 409 when offline or already downloading.

get.description: The studio's notebooks.

post.description: Create an empty notebook.
Upload a Jupyter `.ipynb` file as a new notebook.

get.description: A code run's state and output so far.
A notebook's name and cells.

put.description: Replace a notebook's cells, and optionally its name.

post.description: Commit the notebook to git with a message.

get.description: The notebook as a Jupyter `.ipynb` file.
The notebook's git commits, and whether it has changes since the last one.

post.description: Interrupt the code that is running.

get.description: Whether the notebook's Python is off, starting, idle or busy.

post.description: Restart the notebook's Python, clearing its variables.
Put the notebook back as it was at commit `sha`.

Run code in the notebook's Python and return a run id at once; poll `GET /api/notebooks/runs/{rid}` for the
output. Admins only, because the code runs on the studio's machine with its permissions.
Stop the notebook's Python.
Start the notebook's Python in the background when it is opened, so the first run is quick. Admins only.

get.description: The OS, accelerator and memory, which training and answering backends run here, and why anything is off.
Which hosted providers have a key (never the key itself), the preference-tuning methods, and today's spend.

put.description:
Save (or with `key: null`, remove) the API key for `claude` or `openai`. It is encrypted on this machine
and never shown again. Admins only.

post.description: Send one tiny request to check the key works.

get.description:
One run in full: settings, metrics and their series, events, speed tests, notes, and lineage (data
version, code commit, version stage, where it is deployed).

delete.description:
`what=gguf` deletes the llama.cpp copies only (made again if the version is used), `model` the weights and
copies (the run's record stays), `all` also its logs, metrics and checkpoints. Refused for the version
the agent answers with or serves live, and while it trains or is being copied.

get.description: The last lines of `train.log` (up to 2,000), without progress-bar noise.
One log file when `file` names it (for example `train.log`), otherwise all of the run's logs as a zip.

put.summary: Notes and tags for a run
put.description: Replace a run's notes and tags.

get.description: A CSV showing the format of a safety-check file.
Every account with its role. Admins only.

post.description:
Add an `admin` or `member` account with a temporary password; the person chooses their own at first
sign-in. Admins only.

delete.description: Remove an account and sign out its sessions. You can't remove your own. Admins only.

get.description: The last 100 git commits of the studio's folder and its status.
Whether the studio's folder is a git repository and DVC is set up, and where DVC stores data.
This studio's version and whether a newer release is out (checked once a day, never when offline).

session.name: ak_session
session.description: The session cookie set by `POST /api/login` (12 hours).

csrf.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrf.description: The value of the `tawi_csrf` cookie, sent back on every request that changes something.

keep.description: The indexes of the generated examples to add.

replace.title: Replace
replace.description: Replace the agent's Q&A instead of adding to it.

Agent.description:
An agent as stored in its `bot.json`, without its API key. The most useful fields are listed; others
appear as the agent is used.

id.description: The agent's id (8 hex characters), used in paths as `bid`.

slug.description: The agent's name in the Agent API (`agent` in requests).

qa.description: The example Q&A file's report, split and quality counts.

active_version.description: The version the studio tests with.

api.description: Set once the API exists. The key itself is never returned here.

prompt_sha.description: Fingerprint of the agent file and safety rules.

agent_file_stale.description: The active version was trained on an older agent file.

model_id.title: Model Id
model_id.description: Another base model. Drops the agent's versions.

safety_prompt.title: Safety Prompt
safety_prompt.description: The safety rules added to every conversation.

params.title: Params
params.description: Training settings to change: epochs (0.1 to 50), learning_rate (1e-6 to 1e-2), batch_size and grad_accum (1 to 64), max_seq_length (128 to 8,192), lora_r (1 to 256), lora_alpha (1 to 512), save_steps.

active_version.title: Active Version
active_version.description: The version the studio tests and answers with.

train_engine.title: Train Engine
train_engine.description: The training engine, on NVIDIA GPUs.

content.title: Content
content.description: The agent file's text, up to 20,000 characters.

rate_per_min.title: Rate Per Min
rate_per_min.description: Requests a minute per key (1 to 10,000), or null for the studio default.

daily_limit.title: Daily Limit
daily_limit.description: Requests a day for the agent, or 0 or null for no limit.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: `auto`, `rag`, `model` or `rag+model`, as in the Agent API.

conversation.title: Conversation
conversation.description: A name for the test conversation; the agent remembers its last turns.

version.title: Version

base_model.title: Base Model
base_model.description: Measure the plain base model instead of a fine-tuned version.

command.title: Command
command.description: The command to run (up to 500 characters).

name.title: Name
name.description: A name to show for the source.

secret.title: Secret

root.title: Root
root.description: Notion: only pages whose title contains this.

every_hours.title: Every Hours
every_hours.description: Sync every this many hours (0 = only by hand; up to a week).

target_id.title: Target Id
target_id.description: `local` (this PC) or a connected server's id from `GET /api/compute`.

port.title: Port
port.description: The port the container listens on (1024 to 65535; not 8000 on this PC).

detail.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

request_id.description: The request's id, as in the X-Request-ID header.

n.title: N
n.description: The index build to restore, from `GET /api/bots/{bid}/index-versions`.

key.title: Key
key.description: The API key, or null to remove it.
The new API key, shown only in this response. Store it now.

skip_safety.title: Skip Safety
skip_safety.description: Go live without a passing safety check (recorded on the agent).

must_change.description: The password is temporary and must be changed.

ModelStatus.description: A model and its download state.

style.title: Style

agent_file.title: Agent File
agent_file.description: The agent file's text, instead of the style's template.

new.title: New
new.description: The new password (at least 8 characters, not `admin`).

username.title: Username

embed_model.title: Embed Model
embed_model.description: The embedding model (changing it rebuilds the index).

reset.title: Reset
reset.description: Go back to the default settings.

min_score.description: Passages scoring below this aren't used (0 to 1).

top_k.description: Passages given to the model (1 to 10).

keyword_weight.description: Share of keyword (BM25) search in the hybrid score (0 to 1).

similar_cache.description: Reuse answers for questions this similar (0.85 to 0.99), or 0 for off.

direct_answer.description: Answer straight from an example this similar (0.85 to 0.99), or 0 for off.

pairs.description: Preference pairs the ratings make, for `dpo_human`.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Tags for filtering runs.

key_path.title: Key Path
key_path.description: Path to the SSH private key on the studio's machine.

questions.title: Questions

params.title: Params
params.description: Training settings for this run (kept on the agent); see `params` on the agent.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `qa` (fine-tune on example Q&A), `text` (continued pretraining on raw text) or `align` (preference tuning).

align.title: Align
align.description: For `kind: align`: `method` (`dpo_safety`, `dpo_human`, `dpo_reference`, `dpo_ai` or `ppo`), and optionally `start_version`, `judge` (`claude`, `openai` or `reward_model`) and `steps`.

password.title: Password
password.description: A temporary password (at least 8 characters, not `admin`).

role.title: Role
role.description: `admin` (also manages accounts, servers, notebooks and clearing data) or `member`.

Error400.description: The request can't be done as sent; `detail` says why in a sentence.

Error401.description: Not signed in, or the session has expired.

Error403.description:
The `X-CSRF-Token` header is missing or wrong, the account still has a temporary password and isn't on
the studio's own PC, or (for admin routes) the account isn't an admin.

Error404.description: No such agent (or version, model, notebook or file).

Error409.description: Something else is in the way, usually a training run, download or check already going.

Error413.description: An uploaded file is larger than `TAWI_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` (200 MB by default).

Error429.description: Too many wrong passwords from this address; `Retry-After` says when to try again.

Error500.description: Something went wrong on the server. `request_id` matches a line in the logs.

Error502.description: The connected server couldn't be reached.

Error503.description: The model couldn't answer (it failed to load or ran out of memory).

Error504.description: The command took longer than 60 seconds.
